title: Rich’s “hosting capacity” map became an agency skill tree
summary:
RichDecibels dropped a hand-drawn “Hosting Capacity as a Measure of Agency” chart (group size × duration) and it immediately got treated like a playable skill tree for community builders. The spicy thesis wasn’t the diagram—it was the moral gatekeeping attached to it: Rich’s “individualistic self-development is a scam” and the line that really stuck, “if you can’t create harmonious relationships in a collective of 15 ppl, why should I trust your opinion about policing or governance?” That turned “hosting dinner parties and workshops” into a credibility test for anyone trying to talk big about systems.

Arc-wise: pre-history is the usual “change agents / systems change” lineage (technoshaman’s early tweets, RhysLindmark’s sociotechnical diagrams), then Rich prototypes the problem in 2021 with “Context vs Capacity” (old-timers have context but no spare energy; newcomers have energy but no context, so resentment/polarization blooms). Trigger → peak was Jan 3, 2024: the viral map thread (“long and full of bangers”), plus concrete rules like “never host alone” (power disparity breeds abuse; too much weight on too few shoulders breeds burnout). Peak adoption looked like people literally plotting themselves: Malcolm_Ocean posts his hosting history and asks others to “poast hoasting maps,” MichelleAkin uses it to separate “I don’t want to go further” from “I have yet to go further,” and pepijndevos claims Pepicamp is his “up-rightest thing,” then immediately nitpicks the missing third axis (intensity/load). Patcon_ and rickbenger push the “z-axis” idea too—what’s missing is periodicity/permanence, big-shallow stuff like electoral democracy, and other dimensions like power distribution.

Outcome/current state: nobody really argued the map was wrong; they expanded it, memed it, and built derivatives.
